answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a refundable bond that is slashed on proven misbehavior, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real capital instead of being free. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified work, like a walnut that only yields its kernel after sustained effort, while a nebula of cheap sock-puppet accounts stays dim because none of them can afford the bond or the time to earn trust. One pearl of attested history is worth more than a thousand empty shells, and attackers must pay the bond for every identity they burn.
